name: afanc (avanc)

attributes.attribute: can be tamed by a maiden

sources: Rhys, John. Celtic Folklore: Welsh and Manx. Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1941, 130+.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The afanc, also named the avanc, was a monster of Welsh tale. It haunted a whirlpool in the River Conwy, in north Wales. It could come as a giant beaver, or harder as a crocodile. Its name means a water-dwarf, yet the beast was great. A person could tame it, but only by luring it to the lap of a maiden. It could then be held in chains. One maiden who tried lost her life, for the monster fled back into its lake.
objective: Give an account of the afanc monster.
